Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Petitioner.

parties:
Mokbul Hossain ----- Defendant-Petitioner
Vs.
Khandaker Mujibur Rahman ----- Plaintiff Respondent
full_judgment: 5. As already noticed the defendant-Petitioner lost all through. His learned Advocate-on-Record has only repeated the failed contention that the simple suit for eviction without any prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession is not maintainable. It is not correct to say that the suit was only for eviction of the defendant. It was also for recovery of possession and manse profit. The Courts below have rightly held that the suit as framed was maintainable inasmuch as the plaintiff’s title was admitted by the Government and the defendant was an unauthorized occupant in a portion of the suit land. It appears that the point of maintainability of the suit was not argued in the High Court Division. The only point raised there was that the plaintiff was not able to prove his title in suit plot No. 164. The High Court Division found that the Ministry of Works having released the suit property in favour of the plaintiff and the alleged lease of the defendant from the Deputy Commissioner having been without the approval of the Ministry of Works the defendant had no locus standi to challenge the plaintiff in the suit property however defective it might be.
